segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
And when that king suffered greatly,
and was close to abandoning it and departing,
a certain warrior encouraged him {OCR?}.
And all night the Franks guarded the breach,
and did not allow the Arabs to rebuild it.
And at morning time, the king took the cross and threw it inside the city, and cried out:
"Whoever does not enter with the cross
is stripped of being a Christian!"
And they all leaped and entered the city.
And about fifteen thousand Arabs were killed there in Ascalon,
and the rest fled by ships to Egypt.
And that which is certain is:
in the year 548
548 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1465
1465 of the Greeks,
(1154 of our Lord?), the Franks captured Ascalon;
not as Mar Michael wrote, a year earlier.
And by this victory which the king of Jerusalem achieved,
the lordship of Antioch was rightfully assigned to him,
and he also took as wife the wife of its lord who had died.
And Thoros the Armenian, the ruler of Cilicia, went out {OCR?} to the land of Cappadocia,
and took the Turks captive,
and returned to his country.
And Sultan Mas'ud of Iconium gave his daughter to Ya'qub Arslan,
and they agreed to enter Cilicia.
And because all the watchposts were strongly held by the Armenians,
the Turks turned back in shame from the passes (Clisurae).
And then Thoros grew even bolder,
and took from them the places that remained in the hands of the Greeks.
And Manuel, the emperor of the Greeks, was moved with jealousy,
and sent Andronikos, the commander of the army who was of the royal line, to Cilicia.
And the Armenians and the Franks gathered together,
and met the Greeks at the gate of Tarsus,
and the Greeks were defeated.
And about three thousand of them were killed,
and the rest fled by sea.
And in that same year,
a goat was found that gave birth to a kid that had three {OCR?} eyes and two mouths.
And a severe pestilence occurred in Cilicia and in Iconium.
And in Tishri of that same year,
while men and fair women from the district of Hisn Ziyad were crossing
to come to the feast of Mar Agrippas, which is held in the district of Gubhōs,
a tragedy befell them,
and they were all drowned and choked.
And when many were scandalized,
the teachers of the Church provided consolation in three ways.
